solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go round with Kingsley in haze as one distinctly single-minded?

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word meaning haze

parts.note: a haze is a mist

indicators.note: round tells us to turn the word go back to front

parts.note: taken as written before turning
Kingsley Amis, the English comic novelist

explanation.surface: Someone loiters with Kingsley Amis in a fog, a very single-minded type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses 'Go'; 'single-minded' puns on someone set on staying unmarried, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A misogamist hates marriage, so is resolutely set on staying single, punned as single-minded.

clue.text: Report of girl being unnatural

indicators.note: report of means the word for girl is spoken and we write what is heard

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a girl

explanation.surface: Gossip about a girl's strange behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: MAID and MADE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Made in the sense of man-made or artificial, not occurring in nature.

clue.text: Support American army when environment is evil

indicators.note: the evil word forms the surroundings of the other pieces, as an environment surrounds

parts.note: evil, as a noun, is sin
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Backing the American army when it operates in a wicked setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' is a noun used as a container signal: the evil word surrounds the others. The TA is Britain's volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to hold it up or keep it going, a synonym of support.

clue.text: Sinus-clearing drops will irritate you

definitions.meaning: nasal drops literally travel up into one's nostrils
the idiom for annoying someone intensely

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for annoying someone is read literally as what nasal drops do.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal British idiom meaning to annoy or exasperate someone.

clue.text: Very enthusiastic about university course being planned

indicators.note: about means the enthusiastic word goes round the course

parts.note: mad about something means very keen on it
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a well-known Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A keen student plans out a university course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is a wrap-around signal; PPE is a well-known British degree, Philosophy, Politics and Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Mapped out means planned in detail, as a route is charted on a map.

clue.text: English composer having a very bad upset featured in tabloid

indicators.note: featured in means the reversed pieces are placed within the newspaper

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: ill can mean bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: An English composer has a terrible upset reported in the gutter press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like distress but reverses the pieces (LLIVA); 'featured in' then puts them in The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Sullivan was the English composer of the Gilbert and Sullivan operettas.

clue.text: Fish not happy — caught to be eaten

indicators.note: the letter for caught is swallowed by the word for unhappy

parts.note: sad means unhappy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An unhappy fish is caught and about to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a type of fish, also called horse mackerel.

clue.text: Indian brought into court, one who fought in Burma

indicators.note: brought into says the Indian language is placed inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: Hindi is the main language of India

explanation.surface: An Indian taken into court turns out to be a Burma veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person but is the language HINDI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chindits were Allied special forces who fought behind Japanese lines in Burma in the Second World War.

clue.text: Addict with rest disturbed becomes confused

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of these two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An addict whose sleep is disrupted ends up befuddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges ADDICT and REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Distracted can mean agitated or bewildered, a near synonym of confused.

clue.text: Computer work? Some of the French start to kill time before it

indicators.note: time goes before 'it', the work mentioned earlier

parts.note: des is French for some of the

indicators.note: start to means just the opening letter of kill

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A puzzle about computing, French and killing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to 'work', OP, so T comes before OP at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is a personal computer designed to sit on a desk.

clue.text: English newspaper has stories about socialists maybe

indicators.note: about means the stories word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: lies are stories in the sense of untruths
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A British paper running stories on socialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a wrap-around signal here, not 'concerning'; the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Lefties is an informal word for left-wingers, of whom socialists are an example.

clue.text: Older fashions being recycled shows a reckless lack of wisdom

indicators.note: recycled implies the letters of the two words are used again in a new order

explanation.surface: Bringing back old styles shows foolish recklessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges OLDER and FASHIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardiness is rash boldness, acting without sensible thought.

clue.text: Request from diner resulting in a pudding in perfect condition

definitions.text: Request from diner resulting in a pudding
definitions.meaning: a diner ordering a dessert of baked fruit in pastry
neat and tidy, everything in its place

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally as a restaurant order for a dessert; 'in' links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means everything neat and in perfect arrangement.

clue.text: Bringer of fire could make me 'super-hot'

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of the following words are formed into something else

explanation.surface: A fire-bringer boasts he could make a person extremely hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges ME and SUPERHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Titan stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans.

clue.text: Sequence by that old American writer

parts.note: a run is a sequence, as a run of wins
yon is an archaic word for that

explanation.surface: A series by a past American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon was an American short-story writer known for Guys and Dolls.

clue.text: Disappointing architectural city? Call back

parts.note: Bath is an English city famous for its Georgian architecture

indicators.note: back says the word for call is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to call, as summoning a witness

explanation.surface: Disappointed by a historic city, someone phones back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for call (ETIC). Bath is famous for Georgian crescents, hence 'architectural city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathetic describes an anticlimax, a sudden letdown from the elevated to the trivial.

clue.text: List goes up after match — one plans for the next generation maybe

definitions.text: one plans for the next generation maybe

indicators.note: after places the reversed list behind the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: goes up in a down clue means the list is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A team list is posted after the match, planning for the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' reverses the list in this down clue (ATOR); a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator makes a will, providing for heirs such as the next generation.

clue.text: Ecstasy after bird is seen in spring month? Nonsense!

indicators.note: is seen in places the bird and the drug inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of spring

indicators.note: after puts the ecstasy letter behind the bird

parts.note: a lark is a songbird
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Joy at spotting a bird in May, followed by a dismissive exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the drug behind the bird, and 'is seen in' places both inside the spring month; the exclamation mark belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarkey is informal for nonsense or humbug.

clue.text: I am beginning to plough into heather, making progress with difficulty

indicators.note: into means these pieces go inside the word for heather

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
contracted to I'm

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the first letter of plough

explanation.surface: Ploughing into heathland, someone struggles along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' places the pieces inside ling, a common British name for heather; 'beginning to' takes just the first letter of plough.
explanation.definitionFit: To be limping is to walk lamely, so to advance with difficulty.

clue.text: Mark drinks audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word for drinks is heard rather than seen

parts.note: brews are drinks, especially tea or beer

explanation.surface: A man noisily slurps his drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: BREWS and BRUISE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise is a discoloured mark on the skin.

clue.text: American state with fashionable princess sadly departed

parts.note: in means fashionable
Diana, Princess of Wales, who died in 1997

explanation.surface: A US state mourning a stylish late princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a Midwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: Not involved with filming? There's some compensation

definitions.meaning: away from the film set, read as two words
something that balances out a loss

explanation.walkthrough: 'There's some' simply links to the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An offset is a counterbalancing amount, compensation for something else.

clue.text: Period associated with madness? Ages and ages

definitions.meaning: a spell of time plus a phrase meaning crazy
a very long time, beyond memory

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a time so long ago it is beyond memory.

clue.text: Money in the post, as you might say?

indicators.note: as you might say signals a word that sounds like the phrase for posted

parts.note: something in the post has been sent

explanation.surface: Asking whether cash has been mailed.
explanation.walkthrough: SENT and CENT sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cent is a small coin, a unit of money.

clue.text: Distinguished artist starts to envisage new things

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A renowned artist begins imagining new works.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means famous and respected in one's field.

clue.text: Plumbing problem? Have a word with the servant

parts.note: to see someone is to have a word with them
a page is a young servant

explanation.surface: A householder wants to talk to the servant about a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE PAGE could also mean consult a page in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow escape of liquid, as from a leaking pipe.

clue.text: Pudding — last item for dinners in the past

indicators.note: last item for takes the final letter of dinners

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Pudding was the final course at dinners long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy dessert, typically a milk pudding.

clue.text: Christian favouring only one of Bible's two parts? Not me!

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: Not me means the pronoun is dropped from the Bible section

parts.note: the Old and New Testaments
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Christian who follows only half the Bible protests, insisting it is not them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes ME from TESTAMENT, leaving TESTANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Protestants are members of the Western Christian churches separate from Rome.
